text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The newly-formed coalition government of Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz will present its programme to parliament on Monday.
- Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit says Turkey's development will begin in the impoversished, mainly-Kurdish, southeast.
MILLIYET
- Turkey's far-right Nationalist Action Party elects Devlet Bahceli as party leader after death of former chairman Alparslan Turkes.
- The coalition will provide the financial resources needed for a 35-percent pay rise for civil servants by collecting more taxes and taking credits from domestic and international markets.
HURRIYET
- Interior minister orders full investigation into rumours that the presidential office is being buggged.
- The lower civil servants' salary is 36.7 million Turkish lira after a recent pay rise.
YENI YUZYIL
- Two police intelligence units allegedly used for private purposes by former Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller are being disbanded.
RADIKAL
- State-owned Ziraat Bank endures hardship after being sacrificed for former Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's populist policies.
CUMHURIYET
- Agriculture Minister Mustafa Tasar says Turkey will expand hashish production for industrial purposes.
DUNYA
- Trade courts choked with cases of brand forgery and unfair trading competition.
- Head of Privatisation Board says technically Turkey materialised $850 million in privatisation in a year.
ZAMAN
- The vote of confidence for the new government is expected to be held on Saturday.
- Three people drowned due to floods in the southeast.
